# Running the Model

## Prepare job-specific files

Before each model run, files specific to the target time period must be in place.
This example uses a one-week run:

```
DATE_START="2016-08-27"
DATE_END="2016-09-03"
```

### Restart files

HYCOM and CICE each need a restart file valid at `DATE_START`.

For TP2 hindcast runs, restart files are archived at:

```
/nird/datalake/NS9481K/shuang/TP2_output/expt_02.6/
```

The HYCOM restart file naming convention is `restart.YYYY_DDD_00_0000.[a,b]`, where `DDD`
is the day of year. The CICE restart is `iced.YYYY-MM-DD-00000.nc`.

For example, to start on 27 August 2016 (day 240):

```bash
mkdir -p $WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/expt_<EXPT_ID>/data/cice
cd $WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/expt_<EXPT_ID>/data

cp /nird/datalake/NS9481K/shuang/TP2_output/expt_02.6/restart/restart.2016_240_00_0000.a .
cp /nird/datalake/NS9481K/shuang/TP2_output/expt_02.6/restart/restart.2016_240_00_0000.b .

cd cice
cp /nird/datalake/NS9481K/shuang/TP2_output/expt_02.6/cice/iced.2016-08-27-00000.nc .
```

### Offline nesting files

When offline nesting is enabled in `blkdat.input`, daily archive files must be present in
`$WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/nest/<IEXPT>/` for each day of the run period.

Nesting files for TP2 are at `/nird/datalake/NS9481K/shuang/nest/TP2_expt023/`. If they
are stored as `.tar.gz` archives, the following script extracts the needed files:

```bash
DIR_NST=/nird/datalake/NS9481K/shuang/nest/TP2_expt023
WORK_NST=$WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/nest/<IEXPT>
mkdir -p $WORK_NST
cd $WORK_NST

for (( d=$(date -u -d "$DATE_START" +%s); d<=$(date -u -d "$DATE_END" +%s); d+=86400 )); do
    DATE_NOW=$(date -u -d "@$d" +%Y-%m-%d)
    YYYY=$(date -d "$DATE_NOW" +%Y)
    DOY=$(date -d "$DATE_NOW" +%j)

    afile=archv.${YYYY}_${DOY}_00.a
    bfile=archv.${YYYY}_${DOY}_00.b
    afile_fabm=archv_fabm.${YYYY}_${DOY}_00.a
    bfile_fabm=archv_fabm.${YYYY}_${DOY}_00.b

    # copy directly if files are available individually
    if [ -f ${DIR_NST}/$afile ]; then
        cp ${DIR_NST}/$afile ${DIR_NST}/$bfile .
        cp ${DIR_NST}/$afile_fabm ${DIR_NST}/$bfile_fabm .
        continue
    fi

    # otherwise extract from tar archives
    if [ -d ${DIR_NST}/tar_files ]; then
        for f in ${DIR_NST}/tar_files/archv.${YYYY}_*.tar.gz; do
            range=$(echo "${f#${DIR_NST}/tar_files/archv.${YYYY}_}" | sed 's/\.tar\.gz//')
            start=$((10#${range%_*}))
            end=$((10#${range#*_}))
            if (( DOY >= start && DOY <= end )); then
                tar -xzf ${DIR_NST}/tar_files/archv.${YYYY}_$range.tar.gz $afile $bfile
            fi
        done
        for f in ${DIR_NST}/tar_files/archv_fabm.${YYYY}_*.tar.gz; do
            range=$(echo "${f#${DIR_NST}/tar_files/archv_fabm.${YYYY}_}" | sed 's/\.tar\.gz//')
            start=$((10#${range%_*}))
            end=$((10#${range#*_}))
            if (( DOY >= start && DOY <= end )); then
                tar -xzf ${DIR_NST}/tar_files/archv_fabm.${YYYY}_$range.tar.gz $afile_fabm $bfile_fabm
            fi
        done
    fi
done
```

### Atmospheric forcing files

See [Atmospheric forcing files](external-files.md#atmospheric-forcing-files).

### Prepare the SCRATCH folder

**Note:** This step is also handled automatically by `srjob.sh`. Skip it if you are
using `srjob.sh`.

```bash
cd $WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/expt_<EXPT_ID>
../bin/expt_preprocess.sh ${DATE_START}T00:00:00 ${DATE_END}T00:00:00 $INITFLG
```

A successful run prints a message ending with `No fatal errors. Ok to start model set up in ..`.

## Submit a job

The job script `srjob.sh` handles atmospheric forcing, SCRATCH setup, and job submission
in one step. Open `srjob.sh` in a text editor and update:

| Variable | Example | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `START` | `"2016-08-27T00:00:00"` | Run start time |
| `END` | `"2016-09-03T00:00:00"` | Run end time |
| `INITFLG` | `""` | `""` for a restart run; `"--init"` to initialize from climatology |
| `#SBATCH --time` | `"00:30:00"` | Wall-clock time limit (a 7-day TP2 run takes ~10 min on Betzy) |

Then submit:

```bash
cd $WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/expt_<EXPT_ID>
sbatch srjob.sh
```

Check job status with:

```bash
squeue -u $USER
```

A useful tool for generating SLURM job scripts is available at:
<https://open.pages.sigma2.no/job-script-generator/>

## Check results

When the job finishes, restart files and daily mean files are moved to the `data/` directory.
Confirm successful completion by checking the stop file:

```bash
cat $WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/expt_<EXPT_ID>/log/hycom.stop
```

The file should contain `GOODRUN`. If not, inspect the log files under `log/` for
error messages.

## Visualization

Sample Jupyter notebooks for plotting HYCOM output are available in the
[TP2_setup repository](https://github.com/nansencenter/TP2_setup):

- [plot_2D_TP2_temp.ipynb](https://github.com/nansencenter/TP2_setup/blob/main/plot_2D_TP2_temp.ipynb) — 2D surface maps
- [plot_section_TP2.ipynb](https://github.com/nansencenter/TP2_setup/blob/main/plot_section_TP2.ipynb) — vertical cross-sections

These notebooks read files from `$WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/expt_<EXPT_ID>/data/`.
